driverRegime.method: daily % change of each asset regressed on the daily change in the US 2-year and 10-year yields (basis points) and on the daily % change in WTI; a driver is dominant when |corr| >= 0.4

dataNotes: Run timing: this cycle ran the morning of Friday 13 November 2026 after the GitHub Actions fetch job drafted contracts/*.2026-11-12.json from Thursday 12 November's close. Every figure used is dated at or before 2026-11-12, including Cisco's and Applied Materials' after-hours reactions on the evening of 12 November; news-log entries dated 13 November (October PPI, Nvidia's pre-market rebound, the Microsoft outage, Modine/Cerebras) were NOT used.

Bonds, dollar and IWM sigma are not auto-fetched; the last obtainable implied-volatility values (TLT 30-day IV, EUR/USD 1-month ATM IV, RVX) were carried forward again with stale-source notes. The fetched ^VIX (18.70), ^GVZ (25.91) and ^VXN (28.55) sigma gauges are all dated 12 November.

News-log entries for 2026-11-12 (six, matching the Artifact database exactly; no hand-entered entries) were read. A web search restricted to 12 November session wraps added: breadth, sector returns, VIX, yields, the 30-year auction, dollar/FX, gold/oil closes, credit ETFs and spreads, ETF flows, FedWatch/Kalshi pricing, Hammack's remarks and the after-hours Cisco/Applied Materials reactions (CappNotes 'Closing Look - Thursday, November 12, 2026'; Investrade 'Market Review: November 12, 2026'; Avalon Capital Research 'Market Minute', 12 November; Saxo options brief, 12 November, whose market data is as of 11 November).

Vendor conflicts: the fetched futures closes diverge from the cash-index moves (ES=F +0.43% vs S&P 500 -0.35%; NQ=F +1.08% vs Nasdaq-100 -0.30%; RTY=F -1.26% vs Russell 2000 -1.66%) - the futures settle an hour after the cash close and carry a cost-of-carry basis, and the prior session's futures close preceded part of 11 November's after-hours Nvidia selloff; the fetched closes are used. Some recaps quote stale yields (a MarketAlleys table lists a 4.56% 2-year dated 9 November); the 12 November closes (2Y 4.88%, 10Y 5.10%) from CappNotes, corroborated by Investrade (10Y 5.11%) and Avalon (10Y 5.10%), are used. Saxo's 17.49 VIX is the 11 November close; the 12 November close is 18.70.

Category 1-12 votes are neutral unless a dated source gives a clear read: Breadth (1D, equity assets) is bearish on 12 November's narrow, small-cap-led decline; Rates (1D) are signed on the 2Y +15bp / 10Y +12bp repricing (bearish equities, Treasuries and gold, bullish the dollar); Fed path is horizon-wide and hawkish (December hike fully priced, ~13% for 50bp); the 30-year auction tail is a 1D bearish Positioning vote for Treasuries; Cross-asset (1D) is bearish for the S&P 500, Russell 2000 and gold on the oil jump and firmer dollar. Earnings catalysts are neutral: Nvidia's confirmed CEO change was partly absorbed intraday and Cisco's after-hours gain cuts the other way. Trend structure follows the computed structure reads; Market structure carries its own mechanical direction.

newsLog.event: The WSJ reported Wednesday evening that Nvidia's board is preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang, following the board's investigation into his alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy. The NYT reported a second alleged relationship. Opco, Evercore, William Blair and Bernstein downgraded the stock. NVDA fell about 7.7% pre-market, dragging Nasdaq futures lower and reversing part of Wednesday's AI rally. CoreWeave fell about 10%.
newsLog.numbers: NVDA -7.66% pre-market to $160.43 (vs $173.73 close; about -$321B market cap); Nasdaq-100 futures -0.7% to -1.1%; S&P 500 futures about -0.4% to -0.5%; Dow futures flat; CRWV -9.9%
newsLog.reaction: Puts pressure back on the Nasdaq and the AI trade; uncertainty over leadership and succession, with Q3 results due Nov 17.
newsLog.tickers: NVDA, CRWV, QQQ, Nasdaq, SPY, S&P

newsLog.event: Initial jobless claims for the week ended Nov 7 rose 9,000 to 200,000, slightly above the 195,000 consensus. The 4-week average held at 195,250, its lowest since 1969, and continuing claims fell to 1.697M. The labor market remains tight ahead of the Fed's December meeting, where a rate hike is in play.
newsLog.numbers: Initial claims 200K (prior revised 191K); 4-week avg 195,250; continuing claims 1.697M (-20K)
newsLog.reaction: Minor print. Layoffs stay low, which keeps December Fed-hike risk alive; 10-year yield near 5.00%.

newsLog.event: Overseas markets split: Asia fell as chip names (SK Hynix, TSMC, Advantest) slid on the Nvidia news, while Europe rose despite ASML -3%. Gold dropped about $46 and oil slipped. The 10-year Treasury yield is steady at 5.00% after Wednesday's bond-market holiday.
newsLog.reaction: Gold under pressure with yields pinned at 5%; tech-led weakness in Asia, while Europe holds up.

newsLog.event: Pre-market earnings skew negative. Nebius fell about 11% after pushing its $7B annual sales-pace target from December to February, despite Q3 revenue up 571%. Corteva dropped about 10% on a 9% sales decline, a weaker Brazil outlook and its removal from the MSCI USA index. YETI cut its 2026 guidance. Strategy (MSTR) fell about 6% on its MSCI USA deletion. Wolverine and Teekay Tankers beat.
newsLog.numbers: NBIS -11.4% (Q3 rev $980.8M); CTVA -10.0% (Q3 sales $1.59B, -9%); YETI -8.6% (2026 sales growth cut to ~6% from 7-8%); MSTR -6.1%; WWW Q3 adj EPS $0.79 vs $0.46 est
newsLog.reaction: AI-infrastructure names under pressure alongside Nvidia; single-stock moves otherwise.
newsLog.tickers: NBIS, CTVA, YETI, MSTR, WWW, TNK
newsLog.vsExp: Mixed: NBIS target delayed; WWW and TNK beat; YETI guide cut

newsLog.event: Nvidia confirmed Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, president and director, effective immediately, following the board's investigation into his alleged affairs (including with a suspected Chinese spy). CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO while retaining the CFO title; independent director Harvey C. Jones becomes the board's first chair. No permanent successor has been named; Nvidia still reports Q3 results on Nov 17.
newsLog.numbers: NVDA closed -4.34% to $166.19 (vs $173.73 prior close; intraday low -14.35% to $148.80); Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) -0.54% to 10,506.67, 24 of 30 constituents lower
newsLog.reaction: Stock clawed back roughly two-thirds of its steepest intraday loss after Kress was named interim CEO; CoreWeave fell further (~7%), while AMD (+4.8%) and Broadcom (+5.3%) rose on rotation within AI/semis.
newsLog.tickers: NVDA, SOX, CRWV, AMD, AVGO, QQQ

newsLog.event: US stocks closed lower for a second straight session as the Nvidia leadership shake-up and rate-hike jitters weighed on growth and small-cap stocks; the S&P 500 had opened down nearly 1% before paring losses through the day.
newsLog.reaction: Broad-based weakness led by small caps and semis; October PPI due Friday and the December Fed decision stay in focus with a hike still seen as possible.
